extracted.intended_audience: Indian agents, Department of the Interior officials, reservation administrators, and procurement officers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational criteria for running Indian agencies/reservations: procurement and inspection of supplies, agricultural and irrigation practice, education and missionary work, census and policing, sanitary/hospital care, land allotment and treaty handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment and patent policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments of land at the rate of 160 acres to each head of a family and each adult male; they were to cultivate these allotments for their own benefit, and, as soon as enabled by law to do so, they were to receive patents for such tracts of land conveying to each occupant the fee-simple title to the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement required Indians to remove to reservation, cultivate allotted land, and ultimately receive fee-simple patents when law permitted; supplies and administrative steps were to be provided to effectuate removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discontinuance and reserve disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: It is believed that the best interests require a discontinuance of the Malheur Agency, and the appraisement and sale of the lands included in the reserve, the proceeds of the sale to be invested for the benefit of the Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before action, a thorough investigation of affairs and the condition and disposition of the bands is to be made; recommendations to the department to follow receipt of the special agent's report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peace policy success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical results of the peace policy are measured by Indians being on their reservation and engaged in agriculture and stock-raising, owning implements and household goods, wearing citizens' dress, building houses, erecting churches, operating schools, and producing crops and livestock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative indicators cited include number of implements (mowers, plows, sewing-machines), houses occupied and newly built, acres under cultivation, bushels of wheat/oats/vegetables, tons of hay, number of schools and average attendance, and proportion of wants supplied by government (e.g., less than 10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of surrendering hostiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents were instructed to 'hold out no inducements' to hostile Indians; 'if they come in and surrender their arms and ponies, and submit as prisoners of war, it must be without conditions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance with the presidential order: no promises beyond what the order allows; surrendered groups are to be received and provided for temporarily at specified forts or agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling expirations of treaty annuities
rubrics_metrics.description: When treaty provisions providing annuities for limited years expire, it is important that assistance be continued and early steps taken for permanent settlement upon lands in severalty and for sale of surplus reservation lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to negotiate with tribes to extend benefits appropriate to their present condition; discontinuance of appropriations for schools and other necessary objects would be detrimental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement: bid submission and financial guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: At the annual letting of contracts, proposals must be accompanied by proper certified checks for five per centum of the amount of bid in each case, as required by the act of March 3, 1875, and the rules of the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High compliance expected: e.g., 279 proposals received with over 97% accompanied by the required certified checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract execution and bonding
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts were executed in quadruplicate, and proper bonds furnished for the faithful performance of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts are awarded by the Commissioner with advice from the Board of Indian Commissioners after examination of samples; bonds ensure contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding contracts on sample examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts are awarded after examination of the samples offered by the respective bidders, by competent inspectors or experts appointed for the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample inspection by qualified personnel determines award; department relies on expert assessment of sample quality before acceptance of bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving and warehouse inspection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each package, when delivered at the government warehouse, is weighed, and if found correct the invoice which accompanies the same is properly 'checked.' If a discrepancy exists the same is noted on the invoice, and the necessary correction made on the package itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic receiving includes weighing, invoice checking, noting discrepancies on invoices and packages, followed by expert inspection comparing delivered goods to contract sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert inspection against samples and quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: An inspection by the expert compares the quality of the goods delivered with the sample upon which the contract was awarded, and the number of pounds, yards, or other quantity, with the amount noted on the invoice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection occurs both on entry to and on leaving the warehouse; any nonconforming goods are rejected; rigorous inspection discourages attempts to force inferior supplies upon the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping controls and traceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Shipments are made in a systematic manner, each package being subject to the same scrutiny on leaving the warehouse that it received upon its entry therein. A complete and comprehensive record is kept of the goods received and shipped, so that the office can trace any package that may have gone astray.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record-keeping must be comprehensive enough to account for all packages (example: 26,861 packages with a total weight given, none unaccounted for).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject nonconforming supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy of rejecting all that do not conform to contract requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigid inspection is credited with reducing delivery difficulties and with discouraging contractors from attempting to supply inferior goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement performance indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Fewer difficulties in deliveries and fewer attempts to force inferior supplies indicate better contractor performance, attributed to rigid inspection and known policy of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical delivery compliance and incidence of inferior deliveries as performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrigation infrastructure suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrigation works (e.g., watr-wheel) must be suited to local river peculiarities (rapid, shifting sand-bars, varying rise/fall) and be robustly anchored; permanent dams and properly surveyed ditches are necessary for large-scale cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a 24-ft diameter wheel with specified bucket capacity intended to lift large volumes, but insufficient anchoring led to loss; ditches should be laid out by a competent surveyor to ensure flow and avoid discouraging labor by ineffective results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural development indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure reservation agricultural success by acres under cultivation, crop yields (bushels of wheat, oats, barley, vegetables), tons of hay, and ownership/use of implements (mowers, reapers, plows, harness, wagons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider livestock numbers and condition, number of houses and quality, and local markets for produce as signs of progress toward self-sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education staffing and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary and industrial education are primary means of advancement; teachers must be competent, adequately paid, and supported; cheap/incompetent teachers are not economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation from home influences, instruction in English 'in as thorough a manner as circumstances will admit', industrial/boarding school options (Carlisle/Hampton), and mid-day meals (which increased attendance) are recommended practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational program content and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum emphasis on English language, sewing and garment-making for girls, and industrial training; selection of promising pupils for advanced boarding schools; rapid progress observed when qualified instructors and facilities exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide day and boarding facilities, object-teaching/Kindergarten methods, and consider music and mid-day meals to boost attendance and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue method for rations and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing rations and tools to individuals rather than to captains reduced captain influence and had a good effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution methods should aim to lessen undue influence of village captains and ensure equitable allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Census-taking method
rubrics_metrics.description: Census initially incomplete due to Indian timidity; requiring receipts for rations induced participation leading to an accurate census of those on reserve; subsequent returns increased totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie census-taking to necessary services (e.g., rations) and repeat enumeration to capture absentees; ensure trust-building to avoid undercounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and public-health priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and address principal diseases (e.g., venereal disease/syphilis); hospital facilities must be adequate (avoid flooded or poorly roofed buildings); medical treatment and sanitary rules can reduce prevalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce sanitary rules, improve hospital structures (e.g., shingled roofs), and prioritize medical advice and treatment to address endemic conditions that impede civilization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police organization and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly officered Indian police is valuable for promoting order; they must be efficient, obedient, and ready to reach remote reservation parts; they report violations immediately and enforce agent's orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong police reduces illicit manufacture/sale of 'tiswin' and whisky and helps maintain peace; discipline and impartiality are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation boundary definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reservation boundaries must be distinctly defined at the earliest possible date to prevent trespass and disputes, especially where minerals draw intruders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear legal and surveyed boundaries protect Indian water and land rights and reduce conflicts with miners and settlers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent employment conditions and agency furnishings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents are not encouraged to remain long due to inadequate pay; agency buildings should be furnished with plain, strong, substantial household furniture, as providing permanent furniture would be cost-effective compared to repeated transport costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend more liberal support for agents' pay and for durable agency furnishings to improve retention and agency hospitality burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply contracting quality monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor contract supply quality continuously; example: a poor-quality beef delivery should be remedied by replacing contractor and ensuring sufficient high-quality supplies thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality issues should trigger contractor replacement and closer inspection; maintain records of contractor performance and supply quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary and religious instruction support
rubrics_metrics.description: Where accepted, missionary work and religious instruction are instruments of civilization; local arrangements (alternating preachers, donated materials) support day and Sunday schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage denominational involvement where feasible; donations (books, clothing, instruments) and local preaching in native languages are beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting incidents and handling conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents (murders, attacks) must be reported; military or police action may be invoked when necessary; disposition of offenders may include arrest, local sentencing, or transfer to agency custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of incidents, cooperate with military when required, and ensure policing and justice procedures are enforced to maintain order.
